slides.title: Introduction to URL Routing
slides.content:
# URLs and Views 🔗

Learn how Django routes requests to the right code!

## What you'll learn:
- **URL Patterns** - Mapping URLs to views
- **Path Converters** - Dynamic URL parameters
- **Function-Based Views (FBV)** - Simple view functions
- **Class-Based Views (CBV)** - Powerful view classes
- **URL Namespacing** - Organized URL references

## The Request Flow

```
User Request → URL Router → View → Response
     ↓              ↓         ↓        ↓
  /blog/5/    urls.py    views.py   HTML/JSON
```

> 💡 **URLs are the entry point to your application!** A clean URL structure makes your site more usable and SEO-friendly.

## Django's URL Philosophy

- URLs should be **clean and readable**
- `/article/2024/03/my-post/` ✅
- `/article.php?id=123&year=2024` ❌

slides.title: Basic URL Patterns
slides.content:
# URL Patterns 📍

## Simple Routes

```python
# urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.home, name='home'),
    path('about/', views.about, name='about'),
    path('contact/', views.contact, name='contact'),
]
```

## Corresponding Views

```python
# views.py
from django.http import HttpResponse

def home(request):
    return HttpResponse("Welcome to the home page!")

def about(request):
    return HttpResponse("About us page")

def contact(request):
    return HttpResponse("Contact page")
```

## Including App URLs

```python
# project/urls.py (main)
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('blog/', include('blog.urls')),  # All /blog/* routes
    path('shop/', include('shop.urls')),  # All /shop/* routes
]
```

> 💡 **Best Practice:** Keep app URLs in their own `urls.py` file and include them in the main project URLs.

slides.title: Path Converters
slides.content:
# Dynamic URLs with Path Converters 🔄

## Capturing Values from URLs

```python
# urls.py
urlpatterns = [
    path('article/<int:id>/', views.article_detail),
    path('user/<str:username>/', views.user_profile),
    path('post/<slug:slug>/', views.post_detail),
]
```

## Built-in Converters

| Converter | Matches | Example |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `str` | Any non-empty string (except `/`) | `hello` |
| `int` | Positive integers | `123` |
| `slug` | Slug strings (letters, numbers, hyphens) | `my-post` |
| `uuid` | UUID format | `075194-...` |
| `path` | Any string including `/` | `path/to/file` |

## Using Captured Values

```python
# views.py
def article_detail(request, id):
    # id is automatically an integer!
    article = Article.objects.get(pk=id)
    return render(request, 'article.html', {'article': article})

def user_profile(request, username):
    user = User.objects.get(username=username)
    return render(request, 'profile.html', {'user': user})
```

> 🎯 **Type Safety:** Path converters automatically convert and validate types!

slides.title: Function-Based Views (FBV)
slides.content:
# Function-Based Views 📝

Simple functions that handle requests.

## Basic FBV

```python
from django.shortcuts import render
from django.http import HttpResponse

def home(request):
    return HttpResponse("Hello, World!")
```

## FBV with Template

```python
def article_list(request):
    articles = Article.objects.all()
    return render(request, 'articles/list.html', {
        'articles': articles
    })
```

## Handling HTTP Methods

```python
def contact(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        # Process form data
        name = request.POST.get('name')
        email = request.POST.get('email')
        # Save or send email...
        return redirect('thank_you')
    else:
        # GET request - show form
        return render(request, 'contact.html')
```

## When to Use FBV

- ✅ Simple views with little logic
- ✅ Quick prototyping
- ✅ Custom, unique logic
- ✅ When you need full control

> 💡 **FBVs are explicit and easy to understand!**

slides.title: Class-Based Views (CBV)
slides.content:
# Class-Based Views 🏗️

Powerful, reusable views using classes.

## Basic CBV

```python
from django.views import View
from django.http import HttpResponse

class HomeView(View):
    def get(self, request):
        return HttpResponse("Hello from CBV!")
    
    def post(self, request):
        return HttpResponse("Posted!")
```

## URL Configuration

```python
# urls.py
from .views import HomeView

urlpatterns = [
    path('', HomeView.as_view(), name='home'),
]
```

## Generic Views (Built-in)

```python
from django.views.generic import ListView, DetailView
from .models import Article

class ArticleListView(ListView):
    model = Article
    template_name = 'articles/list.html'
    context_object_name = 'articles'

class ArticleDetailView(DetailView):
    model = Article
    template_name = 'articles/detail.html'
```

## When to Use CBV

- ✅ CRUD operations
- ✅ Reusable, maintainable code
- ✅ Complex views with mixins
- ✅ Following patterns

> 🎯 **Generic CBVs handle 90% of common view patterns!**

slides.title: Common Generic Views
slides.content:
# Built-in Generic Views 📦

## Display Views

```python
from django.views.generic import (
    ListView,     # Display list of objects
    DetailView,   # Display single object
    TemplateView, # Render a template
)

# Simple template
class AboutView(TemplateView):
    template_name = 'about.html'

# List of articles
class ArticleListView(ListView):
    model = Article
    paginate_by = 10  # Built-in pagination!
```

## Editing Views

```python
from django.views.generic.edit import (
    CreateView,   # Create new object
    UpdateView,   # Edit existing object
    DeleteView,   # Delete object
)

class ArticleCreateView(CreateView):
    model = Article
    fields = ['title', 'content']
    success_url = '/articles/'

class ArticleUpdateView(UpdateView):
    model = Article
    fields = ['title', 'content']

class ArticleDeleteView(DeleteView):
    model = Article
    success_url = '/articles/'
```

> 💡 **These views handle forms, validation, and database operations automatically!**

slides.title: URL Naming and Reversing
slides.content:
# URL Names and Reversing 🔙 ## Naming URLs ```python # urls.py urlpatterns = [ path('', views.home, name='home'), path('article//', views.detail, name='article_detail'), path('article/create/', views.create, name='article_create'), ] ``` ## Using Names in Templates ```html Read ❌ Read ✅ Home
``` ## Reversing in Views ```python from django.urls import reverse from django.shortcuts import redirect def my_view(request): # Get URL string url = reverse('article_detail', kwargs={'pk': 5}) # url = '/article/5/' # Redirect to named URL return redirect('home') ``` ## Why Use Names? - ✅ Change URLs without updating templates - ✅ Avoid hardcoded strings - ✅ Self-documenting code - ✅ IDE support and autocomplete

slides.title: URL Namespacing
slides.content: # App Namespacing 📂 Avoid URL name collisions between apps. ## Setting App Namespace ```python # blog/urls.py app_name = 'blog' # Add this! urlpatterns = [ path('', views.list, name='list'), path('/', views.detail, name='detail'), ] # shop/urls.py app_name = 'shop' urlpatterns = [ path('', views.list, name='list'), # Same name, different app! path('/', views.detail, name='detail'), ] ``` ## Using Namespaced URLs ```html Blog Posts Products Article 5 ``` ```python # In views from django.urls import reverse url = reverse('blog:detail', kwargs={'pk': 5}) return redirect('shop:list') ``` > 💡 **Best Practice:** Always use app namespaces in larger projects!

slides.title: Request and Response
slides.content:
# Request & Response Objects 📨 ## The Request Object ```python def my_view(request): # HTTP method method = request.method # 'GET', 'POST' # GET parameters (?name=value) name = request.GET.get('name', 'default') # POST data email = request.POST.get('email') # Headers user_agent = request.headers.get('User-Agent') # User info user = request.user # Current user is_ajax = request.headers.get('X-Requested-With') == 'XMLHttpRequest' # Path info path = request.path # '/blog/article/5/' full_path = request.get_full_path() # includes query string ``` ## Response Types ```python from django.http import ( HttpResponse, JsonResponse, HttpResponseRedirect, Http404, ) # HTML response return HttpResponse("

Hello

") # JSON response return JsonResponse({'status': 'ok', 'data': [1, 2, 3]}) # Redirect return HttpResponseRedirect('/new-url/') # 404 error raise Http404("Page not found") ```
